answer: Identity here is an orchard, not a warehouse. Each account carries a pigment, an outside credential bound to a real anchor, so one human colors one account and it cannot be copied. A hollow identity has no outward links or honest peers; sibling wallets sealed in a closed graph are flagged and pruned. Each epoch a challenge demands a timely signature proving a live operator. A thousand aliases need a thousand credentials, peer links, and timely replies; each extra identity adds cost and another place the graph exposes the farm, so mass forging loses while one honest identity clears every gate.
